newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy union calls Friday strike at Milan airports.
newsitem.headline: Italy union calls Friday strike at Milan airports.

text.p: Italy's SEA, the operating company for Milan's Linate and Malpensa airports, said a trades union representing ground handling staff had called a strike at both airports for Friday June 13 from 0900 to 1300 GMT.
SEA said in a statement it was working to get the planned stoppage called off or, if it went ahead, to reduce disruption to passengers to a minimum.
Many Italians living abroad or away from home are expected to be travelling home on Friday to vote in national referendums on a series of domestic issues to be held next Sunday.

A Milan airport source said the SULTA-CUB union was one of the smaller labour organisations representing workers at Milan's two airports and even if the strike went ahead it was not likely to cause any great disruption.

But negotiations were continuing and it was possible the strike would be called off, perhaps with the intervention of Italy's Transport Ministry which in some cases has the power to forbid labour stoppages.

The trades union is protesting about the planned moving of staff between Linate and Malpensa, productivity, the issue of seasonal and part-time workers and the rights of unions to call meetings. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
